knowledgeAnswers.rationale: An out-of-date reagent can give an unreliable reading. The tester replaces it, takes a fresh sample, retests and records the replacement honestly.
The record must show that no valid test was done and why. Copying or estimating a value creates a false record.
The point is set by the plan and kept the same on each visit so that readings can be compared. Outlet and surface-film samples are not typical of the whole pond.

practicalCriteria: Learner selects the planned sampling point on a simulated pond diagram and states why the filter outlet is not used for a routine reading
Learner labels a simulated sample and records time, location, method, reagent expiry and tester
Learner corrects a planted error with a single line, initials, date and reason, leaving the original entry visible
passRule: Knowledge checks: 80 per cent pass mark. With three questions, all three must be correct. Practical sign-off is assessed separately by observation and is not verified by this quiz.
evidenceRequired: Sample log with time, location, method and tester
Corrected record showing the original entry
Assessor observation of sampling, labelling and recording
stopWorkCriteria: Test reagent or meter is out of date or uncalibrated
The sampling point differs from the client plan and no one has approved the change
Pressure to record a result for a test that was not done
